answer: An agent economy can require each identity to post a stake as hard as quartz, locked through a full voyage of verified work before it earns reputation. A new agent signs each job with its own quill, a unique key, and peers check that stake, work history, and key form one continuous record. Faking one identity is cheap, but faking hundreds means locking capital and doing real work for each, so attack cost scales while an honest agent pays once.
